title: sdd graph proposal payload
description: A batched node proposal for `sdd graph propose`. Observation, claim, red-evidence, consumed-attempt, hash, revision, and origin fields are tool-owned and refused in payloads.

version.description: Payload schema version. This document describes version 1.

nodes.description: The proposed nodes. Order is presentational; execution order derives from deps.

id.description: Stable kebab-case identifier; retired ids are never reused.

contract.description: A falsifiable sentence or two stating what is true when this node is done. A contract that needs paragraphs is a split signal.

justifies.description: The AC-NN / FR-NN / DD-N ids this node exists for. Compile fails when any reachable acceptance criterion has no covering node.

deps.description: Node ids this node depends on. A node becomes workable only when every dep is GREEN.

hazards.description: Triaged failure classes from the closed vocabulary (`sdd graph hazards`). An empty list is a legitimate explicit claim; the string "untriaged" marks an unmade judgment and blocks compile.

artifacts.description: Repo-relative paths this node's implementation writes. Declared write-set: drives parallel-safety and digest anchoring.

estimate.description: Unitless positive relative cost weight (default 1). Consumed only by critical-path analytics and `next` ordering; not a time promise.

phase.description: Presentation grouping for rendered views. No scheduling or review obligation reads it.

role.description: The node's kind of work. Absent means implementation, or review when the gate is a review gate. A review node's deps are the contract nodes it reviews; an integration-acceptance node depends on review nodes and its GREEN closes its whole closure.

history.description: Authored annotation for the human reader (conversion records a v1 task's completion provenance here). Never machine-consumed: states derive from observations alone, and history grants no GREEN.

inputs.description: Declared read-only context this node reads but never writes: whole files, or sections of Markdown files. Compile fingerprints each at embed time; an edit to a declared input later derives INPUT-STALE. Paths resolve against the declared root (repository or planning), never the working directory.

root.description: Which explicit root the path resolves against: the repository root or the planning root. Never the process working directory.

path.description: Root-relative file path (forward slashes). Absolute paths, `..` segments, and symlink escapes are refused.

heading_path.description: A unique suffix of the target heading's ancestry chain: the target heading's title followed by its immediate ancestors' titles in order. The heading plus its nested subsections (until the next same-or-higher level) is selected; a missing or ambiguous match refuses, never falls back.

type.description: How the node's contract is verified. `tests` is the default and strongly preferred; `command` for exit-code truths (builds, linters); `review` for feature gates whose observation is a frozen Aligned review.

tests.description: The runner-reported tests a `tests` gate is satisfied by.

evidence.description: Tests evidence protocol. Absence is legacy; observed-v1 requires an execution profile.

command.description: The check command whose exit code is a `command` gate's observation.

lanes.description: A `review` gate's lane set: "full" (all four lanes; the only form that carries completion-grade closure) or a named subset for lighter checkpoints. The closed vocabulary: review_blind_spots, review_plan_drift, review_quality, review_spec_compliance — compile refuses unknown lane names.

id.description: The test id exactly as the runner reports it.

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file that will define the test.

satisfies.description: Hazards this test discharges. The test's shape must match each hazard's required form, and the merge gate requires it to have been seen failing (red before green).
